title: Fabric-safe ribbon autoscaler: metric composition, capacity quanta, and safety lattice
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Problem: Dedicated fleets need predictable throughput guarantees while minimizing cost. Current autoscalers either oscillate under bursty traffic or are overly conservative, leaving reserved GPUs underutilized. Goal: Implement a policy engine that composes target metrics into a single 'ribbon' decision signal, allocates capacity in discrete quanta (ribbons), and enforces a multi-dimensional safety lattice to prevent unsafe ramping or starved KV cache affinity.

Key concepts: ribbon (single composed target reflecting latency, p95 token throughput, and queue depth), quanta (smallest allocatable capacity unit to preserve model locality), safety lattice (per-tenant + fleet-level constraints: min_capacity, max_delta_per_minute, reversion_windows, and cooldown corridors). The design intentionally avoids continuous fractional scaling to preserve warm KV cache locality and amortize model load costs.
design_notes: Compose signals using a weighted, robust aggregator: Ribbon = median_of_weighted_quantiles([latency_p95, token_rate_per_gpu, pending_requests_ratio]). We choose median_of_weighted_quantiles to reduce sensitivity to outliers in any single signal.
Quanta size defaults: 0.1 GPU equivalent for small tenants, 1.0 GPU for default SKU; configurable by tenant profile. Quanta chosen to balance locality vs. granularity.

Safety lattice levels: tenant_min (hard floor), tenant_max (soft cap), fleet_guard (global emergency ceiling), delta_limit (max quanta change per 60s), and rollback_anchor (previous stable allocation to revert to on instability).

Hysteresis strategy: two windows (fast window=30s, slow window=10min). Fast window for responding to spikes with temporary ribbon lanes that expire; slow window for stable target changes that update allocation and KV affinity policies.

Fallbacks: if ribbon signal conflicts with capacity contract (reserved vs burst), prefer honoring reserved SLAs; when constrained, trigger graceful degradation policies (rate-limit low-priority routes, fall back to smaller quantized model variants).
decisions: Use composed ribbon signal rather than single-metric thresholding to better capture multi-dimensional objectives (latency and throughput).
Allocate in quantized units (quanta) to preserve KV cache hit rates and reduce thrashing.
Implement per-tenant delta limits and a global fleet_guard to stop runaway autoscale loops.
tradeoffs: Quantized allocation improves cache affinity but can increase short-term overprovisioning for fine-grained traffic changes.
Using median_of_weighted_quantiles reduces false positives but can slightly delay reactions to coordinated multi-metric degradations.
Adding the safety lattice reduces oscillation risk but increases policy complexity and onboarding friction for customers who want tight SLAs.
implementation_plan: 1) Policy DSL: extend existing autoscaler DSL to express ribbon composition, quanta, and lattice constraints. (lib/autoscaler/policy_dsl)
2) Signal Aggregator: implement median_of_weighted_quantiles module that consumes time-series windows from metrics pipeline. (service/signal/aggregator)
3) Allocator: implement ribbon_allocator that maps ribbon -> quanta and respects lattice checks. (service/allocator)
4) Safety Controller: enforce delta_limit, rollback_anchor logic with a checkpointed allocation ledger. Persist to leader store. (service/safety)
5) Integration: wire into Dedicated control plane APIs and CLI; add tenant profile knobs for quanta sizing. (api/dedicated)
6) Tests: unit tests for aggregator math, property tests for allocator under synthetic workloads, and e2e with canary tenant.
testing_plan: Unit tests: edge cases for quantile composition and weight drift.
Property tests: invariants (never exceed tenant_max, never violate delta_limit) under randomized inputs.
Load simulations: replay representative traffic traces (low-burst, heavy-burst, diurnal) to validate no oscillation and acceptable p95 latency targets.
Chaos tests: leader failure and network partition to ensure allocations reconcile correctly after recovery.
Canary: 1% traffic on staging fleet -> 5% on a dedicated canary fleet with detailed telemetry retention.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Merge feature flags and internal tests; keep disabled by default. Monitor CI coverage.
Phase 1: Enable for internal Redwood teams on Dedicated staging (two tenants) for 2 weeks; verify no SLA regressions.
Phase 2: Open beta for selected customers with support contact; apply tenant profile tuning with SRE assistance.
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to GA: 25% fleets -> 50% -> 100% with 24h observation windows and quick rollback flags.
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert if allocation_delta > delta_limit for 3 consecutive minutes: autoscaler.delta_breach
Alert if ribbon_signal variance > 2x baseline in 1 minute: autoscaler.ribbon_spike
SLO: maintain p95 latency <= configured target for 95% of 1h windows; create regression alert if breached post-deploy.
Dashboard: per-tenant ribbon, allocated_quanta, KV_cache_hit_rate, and rollback_count; include annotation stream for policy decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Ribbon signal implemented and unit-tested with deterministic results for synthetic series.
Allocator respects quanta and safety lattice invariants under fuzz testing.
No sustained SLA regressions in internal staging canary (p95 within 1.1x baseline and no more than 2 rollbacks in 24h).
Documentation updated (policy DSL reference and tenant profile guide) and migration script for existing autoscaler configs provided.
